title: Homothety and unbounded evaluation give canonical coherent biduality
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and work in the ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], using derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site and derived tensor computed by K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $L\in D(R)$ be isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $R$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Suppose the scalar-action morphism $h:R[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)$, adjoint to the unit action on $L$, is an isomorphism. For every $K\in D(R)$ whose cohomology modules are finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] in every degree, without a boundedness assumption, the evaluation comparison
$$e_{K,L,L}:R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),L)$$
is an isomorphism. Here $e$ is the transpose of the map that first evaluates the $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$ and $K$ factors into $L$ and then evaluates $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)$ into $L$, using the graded symmetry to order the factors. The composite
$$K\cong R[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{h\otimes 1}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{e_{K,L,L}}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),L)$$
is exactly the canonical biduality morphism $\delta_K$ adjoint to evaluation $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to L$. Thus $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism in $D(R)$, naturally in $K$. No finite-generation assumption on the cohomology of $L$ is required.

proof.text: For each integer $n$, the good truncation $K_n=\tau_{\leq n}K$ has $H^j(K_n)=H^j(K)$ for $j\leq n$ and zero for $j>n$: replace degree $n$ by the kernel of the outgoing differential and delete higher degrees. Thus $K_n$ is bounded above and all its cohomology modules are finitely generated. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] over the given Noetherian ring shows that every $K_n$ is pseudo-coherent. This does not impose a bound on $K$ itself.

proof.text: Put $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] on the small one-object site with trivial topology and coefficient ring $R$. Its tensor unit is $R[0]$. For every module $N$, the assumed isomorphism $h$ gives $T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]\cong R[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]\cong N[0]$. Consequently $T$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. The bounded injective representative assumed for $L$ supplies finite injective dimension for both copies of $L$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-finite-injective] with its $(K,L,M)$ equal to $(K,L,L)$. Step 1 supplies all pseudo-coherent truncations, and Step 2 supplies finite injective dimensions and finite Tor dimension. It follows that the specified canonical comparison $e_{K,L,L}$ is an isomorphism. No finiteness of the cohomology of $L$ was used.

Write $B=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$, let $\epsilon_{X,Y}:R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}X\to Y$ denote evaluation, and let $\lambda$ denote the left unitor. Set $b=e_{K,L,L}\circ(h\otimes1_K)\circ\lambda_K^{-1}$. By [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], uncurrying $b$ with $B$ on the left gives, with the specified graded symmetry and associators, $\epsilon_{L,L}\circ(h\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\lambda_{B\otimes K}^{-1}$. Since $h$ is adjoint to the unit action, $\epsilon_{L,L}\circ(h\otimes1_L)=\lambda_L$. The uncurried map is therefore $\lambda_L\circ(1_{R[0]}\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\lambda_{B\otimes K}^{-1}=\epsilon_{K,L}$ by naturality of the unitor. The adjunction bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], composed with symmetry, is injective, so $b=\delta_K$. All three factors of $b$ are isomorphisms; hence so is $\delta_K$. Naturality of $e$, of $\lambda$, and of tensoring the fixed map $h$ makes $b=\delta$ natural in $K$.

Step 1: each good truncation tau<=n K is bounded above with finitely generated cohomology, so the cited Noetherian criterion (066E (2)) makes it pseudo-coherent; this is the same pseudo-coherence notion as condition (iii) of the 0A69 node. Step 2: the closed monoidal node on the one-object site gives T⊗N[0] ≅ R[0]⊗N[0] ≅ N[0] through h, so T has Tor amplitude [0,0]; the bounded injective L gives condition (i). Step 3: lem-trf-derived-evaluation-finite-injective applied to (K,L,L), matching Stacks 0A69's three hypotheses as checked in more-algebra.tex. Step 4: I redid the uncurrying. It uses the B-first composite of the canonical-map node, eps∘(h⊗1)=lambda (from the closed node's u <-> eps∘(u⊗1)) and naturality of the unitor, so the uncurried map is eps_{K,L} and b = delta_K, natural in K. This makes explicit the identification K = RHom(ω,ω)⊗K that the proof of 0A7C leaves implicit; 0A7C's finite cohomology of ω is needed only for D_Coh preservation, so dropping it is correct. Edge cases checked: Z with L=[Q→Q/Z] and K=Z/2; a field with unbounded K; K=0; L=0. No duplicate: finite-module-canonical-biduality is the special case K=M[0] and cites this item; sf-dualizing-complex-bounded-duality is narrower; derived-evaluation-pseudocoherent has different hypotheses. lean.statement: theorem homothety_evaluation_biduality (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hL : ∃ J : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ, (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (J.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Injective (J.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (Q.obj J ≅ L)) (hh : IsIso ((singleFunctorObjUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u} R)).hom ≫ MonoidalClosed.id L)) : (∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R), (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K)) → IsIso (homothetyEvaluationComparison R K L) ∧ (λ_ K).inv ≫ (singleFunctorObjUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u} R)).inv ▷ K ≫ (((singleFunctorObjUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u} R)).hom ≫ MonoidalClosed.id L) ▷ K) ≫ homothetyEvaluationComparison R K L = homothetyCanonicalBidual R K L ∧ IsIso (homothetyCanonicalBidual R K L)) ∧ (∀ (K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : K ⟶ K'), (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K)) → (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K')) → f ≫ homothetyCanonicalBidual R K' L = homothetyCanonicalBidual R K L ≫ (ordinaryModuleDerivedInternalHom R).map (((ordinaryModuleDerivedInternalHom R).map (f.op, 𝟙 L)).op, 𝟙 L))
